Below is a comprehensive pytest test-suite that exercises the function `is_balanced_parens`.  
It covers:

• Happy-path scenarios (different balanced patterns, nesting, interspersed characters, large input).  
• Edge-cases (empty string, single bracket, only non-bracket characters, etc.).  
• Error-cases (input that is not a string / not iterable, which should raise `TypeError`).

Save the code in e.g. `test_is_balanced_parens.py`.

```python
import pytest

# Replace the import below with the real location of the function
# from my_package.my_module import is_balanced_parens
from balanced_parens import is_balanced_parens   # example path


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Happy-path tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text",
    [
        "()",           # single pair
        "()[]{}",       # several independent pairs
        "({[]})",       # nested
        "([{}])",       # deeply nested
        # mixture of brackets and ordinary characters
        "if (arr[0] == '{') { return true; }",
        # very large, but still balanced
        "(" * 10_000 + ")" * 10_000,
    ],
)
def test_balanced_inputs_return_true(text):
    assert is_balanced_parens(text) is True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Edge-case tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text, expected",
    [
        ("", True),        # empty string
        ("abcXYZ", True),  # no bracket characters at all
        ("(", False),      # single opening
        (")", False),      # single closing
        ("(()", False),    # one missing closing
        ("())", False),    # one extra closing
        ("([)]", False),   # cross-order mismatch
        ("[(])", False),   # another crossing
    ],
)
def test_edge_cases(text, expected):
    assert is_balanced_parens(text) is expected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Error-case tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_input", [None, 42, 3.14, object()])
def test_non_string_input_raises_type_error(bad_input):
    """
    The function iterates over the input.  Non-iterable inputs
    (or inputs that are not strings) should raise TypeError.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        is_balanced_parens(bad_input)
```

Explanation of coverage:

• `test_balanced_inputs_return_true` ensures that a variety of correct, possibly large inputs are accepted.  
• `test_edge_cases` checks boundary conditions and common failure modes (missing / extra / crossed brackets, empty string, strings with no brackets).  
• `test_non_string_input_raises_type_error` guarantees the function fails fast on obviously unsupported argument types, exercising the error path triggered by Python’s own iterator protocol.
